findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_recipe_build_activity, search_recipes · Private data: get_recipe_build, get_run, review_recipe_build, run_recipe_acceptance, start_recipe_build, update_recipe_build · Public sink: commit_recipe_build · Destructive: check_recipe_build, discover_stewai, get_results, get_run, review_recipe_build, run_recipe, run_recipe_acceptance, search_recipes.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_recipe_build_activity, search_recipes · Private data: get_recipe_build, get_run, review_recipe_build, run_recipe_acceptance, start_recipe_build, update_recipe_build · Public sink: commit_recipe_build · Destructive: check_recipe_build, discover_stewai, get_results, get_run, review_recipe_build, run_recipe, run_recipe_acceptance, search_recipes

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_results" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
